selection_contract.authority_basis: Every declaration in candidate_universe is read from the exact committed HEAD:verification/comparator.json roster; uncommitted Comparator edits, roster order, and ease of qualification are not selection evidence.

ranking_axes.test: Prefer a substantive theorem or obstruction with a real mathematical mechanism over a routine identity, finite instance, or renamed transport.
Prefer a direct consequence for an Erdős target or a faithful exact reduction to its remaining endpoint, while keeping any missing producer explicit.
Expose the hard certificate, averaging, recurrence, or obstruction step and the hypotheses that make it work; do not flatten friction into a headline.
Prefer a result that adds a distinct mathematical route or support class rather than a corollary or duplicate wrapper.
Prefer a statement whose exact scope, source attribution, and significance can be checked by a reader without reconstructing hidden context.
Prefer a result that teaches a reusable mechanism and connects the source theorem to the open boundary.
Require an exact current source declaration, committed Challenge transport, and source-checked hypotheses and conclusion.
Penalize hidden conditionality, missing cofinal supply, and language that could be read as solving a still-open problem.

selection_contract.anti_underclaim_boundary: Do not select a timid proxy merely because it is easy to qualify: an unconditional direct theorem with a visible hard mechanism must remain eligible even when it is classical or leaves the universal problem open.
selection_contract.anti_hype_boundary: No selected result closes universal Erdős #257 or any other open programme; exact hypotheses, prior-art attribution, proof authority, limitations, and the surviving open boundary remain part of the result.
selection_contract.reversal_evidence: Reverse the choice only if a newly committed, source-checked Comparator row has a strictly stronger direct consequence at the same or closer endpoint, genuinely deeper independent mechanism, equal-or-better evidence certainty, and no larger hidden-hypothesis or overclaim risk; uncommitted dirt or a row count cannot reverse it.

candidate_selection.statement: For every integer base b >= 2, the full-support Erdős–Borwein series sum over k >= 0 of 1/(b^(k+1)-1) is irrational.
candidate_selection.open_boundary: This proves the full-support series only; irrationality for every infinite support in Erdős #257 remains open.
candidate_selection.hard_mechanism: The source proof closes a weighted divisor-block certificate pipeline: a bounded Bertrand/CRT first-block frame, middle-window divisor-pair averaging with pigeonhole selection, weighted tail control, and explicit parameter closure. The local theorem is the final consumer of that completed machine.
candidate_selection.why_this_is_the_showcase: It is the strongest direct and unconditional endpoint result in the committed Comparator spine: a canonical full-support member of Erdős #257 with a visible completed mechanism and a clean statement-isolated Challenge type. Its classical attribution is disclosed, not hidden, and does not diminish its review value.
candidate_selection.attribution: The source docstring records Erdős (1948) for the full-support theorem; the local Lean proof is the proof authority, while the cited source and repository prior-art ledger supply attribution and statement-fidelity context.
limitations: It proves only the full-support series, not irrationality for every infinite support.
It does not solve universal Erdős #257.
The base condition b >= 2 is part of the theorem and no other base or support interpretation is implicit.
Comparator establishes statement identity and configured axiom use, not novelty or editorial significance.

selection_comparison.reason: It is the nearest alternative and remains a high-value distinct result, but its infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses cover a narrower support class; the selected full-support theorem has the more canonical direct endpoint and a completed divisor-block certificate pipeline.

Its bouquet and uniform tail-selection hypotheses expose a deeper conditional route, but those structural hypotheses are not constructed for arbitrary supports; its evidence boundary is therefore weaker for an unconditional showcase.
It is a sharp, useful no-go result, but it excludes one proof architecture and concludes no irrationality statement; it is lower consequence for the selected Palomar candidate.
It is an exact #68 endpoint reduction with excellent review value, but its cofinal non-unit-carry producer remains unproved; an equivalence to the open endpoint is not a direct irrationality result.

It is a deep independent #249 structural theorem, but infinite-dimensional kernel rank is farther from the irrationality endpoint than the selected direct result and does not supply the missing unbounded certificate family.
